Subject: Tundra AI — GPU pool topology and burst autoscale criteria

Hi team / Aisha,

Following our intake call last week, I sketched a first-pass GPU pool topology and a proposed autoscale/burst criteria set for Tundra's Dedicated capacity. Attached: tundra_pool_topology_v1.pdf and a CSV with threshold suggestions. High-level asks:

- Confirm primary regions: us-west1 (primary) and us-east4 (failover/burst).
- Approve baseline pool sizes for inference and fine-tuning traffic (see topology doc).
- Confirm acceptable burst window (30min sustained vs 10min spikes) and max burst-to-baseline multiple.
- Identify any procurement or security gating (KMS, required IP ranges) we should pre-provision.

I put Ben and Grace on this thread to ensure commercial alignment and CS/implementation sequencing. Rishi, can you validate the autoscale knobs below against our current fleet limits? If we can lock these by Thursday we can schedule a kickoff and netops ticket.

Proposed autoscale defaults (in CSV):
- scale_up_threshold: 70% GPU util over 2m average
- scale_down_threshold: 35% over 5m average
- burst_multiplier: 3x baseline for 10m spikes, 1.5x for sustained 30m windows
- prewarm_count: min(2, 10% of baseline)

Thanks — Kim

--

Appreciate the diagram, Kim. A couple implementation points from CS/implementation:

- Implementation sequencing: network -> KMS -> pool provisioning -> model warmup -> traffic cutover. We need NETOPS ticket with required CIDR ranges at least 5 business days before provisioning.
- Migration plan: start with a canary namespace (2 GPUs) in us-west1, run traffic mirror for 48h, then expand to baseline.
- Observability: please add these metrics to the topology doc: per-route latency p50/p95, queue depth, token/sec, and per-GPU memory pressure. We'll want alert thresholds tied to autoscale events.
- Data retention: Tundra asked for 30 days of trace retention at pilot; confirm storage costs (Ben — will this be in the base or as add-on?).

I mapped the milestones to the kickoff deck (link below). If procurement confirms capped burst we can schedule the kickoff next week.

Regards,
Grace

Quick infra check after reviewing the attachments:

- Baseline/Pool sizing: us-west1 baseline 18 A100-eq is fine. For us-east4 failover, we can keep a warm standby of 6 GPUs (fast failover) but only enable bursting from that region during low-cost windows to control cross-region egress.
- Autoscale knobs: the proposed thresholds look sane. Couple of tweaks I recommend:
  * scale_up_threshold -> 65% over 3m to reduce flip-flop on short spikes
  * burst_multiplier: allow 3x for 5m spikes but require manual approval for sustained >30m bursts outside pilot
  * prewarm: prefer prewarmed instances for stateful models; containers are cheaper for stateless inference.
- Monitoring labels: add \"pool: tundra-prod\", \"region: us-west1\", \"tier: baseline|burst\" to all metrics so the Console dashboards can filter cleanly.
- Netops: I'll open the NETOPS ticket with the CIDRs needed and include a sample firewall rule. Aisha — can you confirm whether KMS will be customer-managed or Redwood-managed? If customer-managed, we need the key ARN by provisioning.

I'll be available for a 30m sync Thursday morning PT.

Rishi
